SMTO-SKL-0186 — This GitHub file transfer needs a Conversation

GUID: c460b8fe-0939-50ee-a936-082056764539
Slug: github-artifact-context-required
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • SMTO saves GitHub downloads, and reads GitHub uploads, from the files of an active Conversation. This request ran without one, so there was nowhere to keep the file. Nothing was transferred.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open a Conversation with the Agent (or start a new one) and ask for the GitHub download or upload there. Only a Conversation has a place to keep the files that come from or go to GitHub.
  2. For an upload, attach the file to that Conversation first, using the Add context button next to the message box and then Add files to conversation. SMTO only uploads files that belong to the Conversation you are in.
  3. If you were already in a Conversation, open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. Inside a Conversation this shouldn't happen, so the details help find the cause.

What success looks like

  • The downloaded file appears in the Conversation, or the Agent confirms the upload.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO and say where you made the request.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A GitHub file transfer (download or release asset upload) ran without the run's artifact registry or without both run_id and conversation_id in its artifact scope, so there was nowhere to read or save files.

What this means

  • File transfer lacks an ArtifactStore registry or active run/conversation scope. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • File transfer lacks an ArtifactStore registry or active run/conversation scope.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the active artifact context before upload or download.

How to fix it

  • Invoke the transfer from an Agent run inside a conversation, where artifacts.runtime.bind supplies _artifact_store and _artifact_scope (run_id, conversation_id). If this happens inside a normal Agent conversation, treat it as a runtime wiring defect and capture the Server log.
  • Run the transfer in a conversation with an active ArtifactStore run scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended transfer runs with valid conversation ownership.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
